---
title: "Resources"
order: 11
---

External links for this lesson. All checked to load from a plain request as of the date this
page was written. (Note: eCFR's and fda.gov's own rendered sites block automated/proxied traffic
with a bot check in this repo's build environment, even though a human browser reaches them fine;
the regulation text quoted in this lesson comes from eCFR's public Versioner API instead, and the
links below use verified-loading mirrors of the same official text.)

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 606.100, current text](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.100)**
  — the standard operating procedures requirement this lesson applies to BECS directly. Use this
  to check the current text, since regulations get amended and the copy in this repo's `sources/`
  folder is a dated snapshot.

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 11.10, current text](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/11.10)** —
  the "controls for closed systems" section, including the systems-validation clause this lesson
  quotes. This module names Part 11 only briefly; Track 3 (`csv-and-becs`) covers the full
  electronic-records framework this section sits inside.

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 606.171, current text](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.171)**
  — the biological product deviation reporting section this lesson applies to a software defect,
  already covered in full in the `risk-and-controls-vocabulary` foundation lesson.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)** — the
  U.S. Government Publishing Office's official, legally authoritative annual CFR archive. Use this
  for the official, dated, legally citable version of a specific year's text — for example, to
  confirm exactly what a section said on the date of a past inspection or a vendor change.

- **[#26 Computer System Validation (CSV)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QPhXYSOLgjM)** (Waters
  Corporation, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. A general
  computer-system-validation explainer from a major life-sciences/analytical-instrument company,
  not blood-specific or BECS-specific and not tied to any CFR citation here — use it for the
  broader "why does a regulated computer system need this much scrutiny" concept that 11.10(a)
  states in one sentence, which this module applies specifically to BECS. Verified embeddable via
  YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **AABB Standards, Section 3.9, "Information Systems"** — not independently link-verified this
  session (see `sources/aabb/information-systems-section-3.9.md` for how its section number and
  themes were cross-confirmed). This is AABB's own accreditation-side counterpart to this lesson's
  FDA-side validated-state discussion: records/validation, backup/continuity, personnel
  responsibility, documented change processes, and access control, checked by an AABB assessor
  rather than an FDA investigator. Start from
  **[AABB: Standards for Blood Banks and Transfusion
  Services](https://www.aabb.org/standards-accreditation/standards/blood-banks-and-transfusion-services)**
  (verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11, HTTP 200) for the current catalogue page; the full
  standard text itself sits behind AABB's member/purchase access, so don't expect the free page to
  show Section 3.9's actual requirement language.

- **[FDA: Blood Establishment Computer System Validation in the User's
  Facility](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/blood-establishment-computer-system-validation-users-facility)**
  — FDA/CBER's own guidance document page for the exact guidance this lesson names but couldn't
  confirm a live link for in an earlier session; now verified loading directly. Use this to check
  the current version and issue date before citing it in a real Lakeshore document — this module
  deliberately stops at *why* BECS validation matters, not *how* to run it, and this is where the
  "how" guidance actually lives. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Software as a Medical Device
  (SaMD)](https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/digital-health-center-excellence/software-medical-device-samd)**
  — FDA's own Digital Health Center of Excellence page on software that meets the FD&C Act's
  medical-device definition, the general framework behind this lesson's point that some BECS
  products are themselves FDA-regulated medical devices, cleared through premarket review, quite
  apart from Lakeshore's own CGMP obligations. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP
  200).

- **[ISPE: GAMP 5 Guide (2nd
  Edition)](https://www.ispe.org/publications/guidance-documents/gamp-5-guide-2nd-edition)** — the
  International Society for Pharmaceutical Engineering's own catalogue page for GAMP 5 (Good
  Automated Manufacturing Practice), the industry-practice-tier risk-based validation framework
  this lesson names but deliberately doesn't teach — that's Track 3's (`csv-and-becs`) job. Use
  this to see GAMP 5 as ISPE itself describes it, not a secondhand summary. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 301 → 200 on the redirected URL).
